scenarioStory.history: Patient was tackled during a rugby match and landed on an outstretched right arm. He immediately felt his shoulder "pop out" and has been unable to move it since. Reports severe pain rated 9/10, worse with any attempted movement. Denies numbness initially but now reports mild tingling in the fingertips.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 22-year-old male seated on the sideline, holding his right arm, with an obviously deformed right shoulder following a rugby collision. → Neurovascular assessed, splinted, pain treated: Crew completes a focused assessment of the extremity, confirms distal pulse/sensation/movement, splints the shoulder in the position found, and administers IV morphine dosed to the patient's weight while monitoring vital signs for respiratory depression or hypotension. → Pain reassessed, BP stable, ready for transport: Patient is splinted, pain is improving, and vital signs remain stable. Crew transports in a position of comfort with continued reassessment.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Right shoulder pain and deformity after a rugby collision

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 22-year-old male seated on the sideline, holding his right arm, with an obviously deformed right shoulder following a rugby collision.

scenarioEvents.name: Neurovascular assessed, splinted, pain treated
scenarioEvents.description: Crew completes a focused assessment of the extremity, confirms distal pulse/sensation/movement, splints the shoulder in the position found, and administers IV morphine dosed to the patient's weight while monitoring vital signs for respiratory depression or hypotension.
relatedChecklist: Assess distal pulse, sensation, and movement of right arm before splinting
Assess pain using Numeric Rating Scale (patient is 22 years old)
Morphine 8 mg IV (82 kg × 0.1 mg/kg = 8.2 mg, rounded to 8 mg; max initial dose 10 mg)
Splint shoulder/arm in position found; do not force reduction
Monitor SpO2 and respiratory rate closely after morphine for signs of hypoventilation

scenarioEvents.name: Pain reassessed, BP stable, ready for transport
scenarioEvents.description: Patient is splinted, pain is improving, and vital signs remain stable. Crew transports in a position of comfort with continued reassessment.
relatedChecklist: Reassess pain score and vital signs after morphine administration
Transport in position of comfort with continued reassessment

scenarioEvents.name: Morphine given without BP reassessment
scenarioEvents.description: The crew administered morphine but did not reassess blood pressure or respiratory status afterward. The patient becomes hypotensive and mildly drowsy, an under-recognized opioid effect that a timely reassessment would have caught.
relatedChecklist: Recognize opioid-related hypotension/sedation; reassess vitals and titrate care
